eslint:@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars.explanation: A variable, function or parameter is declared but never used.
eslint:@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars.recommendation: Remove it or use it as intended.
eslint:@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars.severity_rationale: Dead code; may indicate incomplete logic.
eslint:@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars.title: Unused variable

eslint:eqeqeq.explanation: == and != coerce operand types (e.g. '' == 0 is true).
eslint:eqeqeq.title: Loose equality (== / !=)

eslint:no-async-promise-executor.explanation: new Promise receives an async function.
eslint:no-async-promise-executor.recommendation: Use a regular executor or an async function without wrapping.
eslint:no-async-promise-executor.severity_rationale: Errors thrown in the async executor are lost.
eslint:no-async-promise-executor.title: Async Promise executor

eslint:no-compare-neg-zero.explanation: Comparing against -0 does not distinguish signed zero.
eslint:no-compare-neg-zero.title: Comparison with -0

eslint:no-cond-assign.explanation: An assignment operator appears in a conditional test.
eslint:no-cond-assign.recommendation: Use a comparison operator or move the assignment out.
eslint:no-cond-assign.title: Assignment in condition

eslint:no-constant-condition.explanation: A condition is a constant expression.
eslint:no-constant-condition.recommendation: Use a real condition or remove the dead branch.
eslint:no-constant-condition.severity_rationale: The branch always or never executes.
eslint:no-constant-condition.title: Constant condition

eslint:no-debugger.explanation: A debugger statement is left in source.
eslint:no-debugger.severity_rationale: Pauses execution in developer tools; should not ship.
eslint:no-debugger.title: debugger statement

eslint:no-dupe-else-if.explanation: An else-if chain repeats a condition already tested.
eslint:no-dupe-else-if.recommendation: Fix the condition or remove the dead branch.
eslint:no-dupe-else-if.severity_rationale: The duplicated branch can never run.
eslint:no-dupe-else-if.title: Duplicate else-if condition

eslint:no-dupe-keys.explanation: An object literal defines the same key twice.
eslint:no-dupe-keys.recommendation: Remove or rename the duplicate key.
eslint:no-dupe-keys.severity_rationale: The later key silently overwrites the earlier one.
eslint:no-dupe-keys.title: Duplicate object key

eslint:no-duplicate-case.explanation: A switch has two identical case expressions.
eslint:no-duplicate-case.recommendation: Remove or correct the duplicate case.
eslint:no-duplicate-case.title: Duplicate case label

eslint:no-empty.explanation: A block statement (including catch) is empty.
eslint:no-empty.recommendation: Implement the block, handle the error, or add a comment explaining why it is empty.
eslint:no-empty.severity_rationale: Often a swallowed error or unfinished logic.
eslint:no-empty.title: Empty block

eslint:no-eval.explanation: eval() runs a string as JavaScript with the caller's privileges.
eslint:no-eval.recommendation: Remove eval; use JSON.parse, lookup tables or explicit functions.
eslint:no-eval.severity_rationale: Executes arbitrary strings as code; injection risk.
eslint:no-eval.title: Use of eval()

eslint:no-fallthrough.explanation: A case falls through without break/return.
eslint:no-fallthrough.recommendation: Add break/return or an explicit fall-through comment.
eslint:no-fallthrough.severity_rationale: Unintended execution of the next case.
eslint:no-fallthrough.title: Switch case fall-through

eslint:no-implied-eval.explanation: setTimeout/setInterval/execScript receive a string that is evaluated.
eslint:no-implied-eval.recommendation: Pass a function instead of a string.
eslint:no-implied-eval.severity_rationale: Strings passed to timers are evaluated as code.
eslint:no-implied-eval.title: Implied eval (string passed to setTimeout/setInterval)

eslint:no-loss-of-precision.explanation: A numeric literal exceeds double precision.
eslint:no-loss-of-precision.recommendation: Use a representable value or BigInt.
eslint:no-loss-of-precision.severity_rationale: The literal cannot be represented exactly at runtime.
eslint:no-loss-of-precision.title: Number literal loses precision

eslint:no-new-func.explanation: The Function constructor compiles code from strings at runtime.
eslint:no-new-func.title: new Function() constructor

eslint:no-prototype-builtins.explanation: hasOwnProperty etc. are called directly on the target object.
eslint:no-prototype-builtins.severity_rationale: Fails for objects without a prototype or with shadowed methods.
eslint:no-prototype-builtins.title: Object.prototype method called on object

eslint:no-script-url.explanation: A javascript: URL executes code when navigated.
eslint:no-script-url.recommendation: Use event handlers instead of javascript: URLs.
eslint:no-script-url.severity_rationale: Equivalent to eval in navigation contexts; XSS vector.
eslint:no-script-url.title: javascript: URL

eslint:no-self-assign.explanation: A variable is assigned to itself.
eslint:no-self-assign.severity_rationale: Has no effect; usually a typo.
eslint:no-self-assign.title: Self assignment

eslint:no-self-compare.explanation: A value is compared with itself.
eslint:no-self-compare.recommendation: Compare the intended values; use Number.isNaN for NaN checks.
eslint:no-self-compare.severity_rationale: Always true/false; usually a typo (except NaN checks).
eslint:no-self-compare.title: Comparison with itself

eslint:no-sparse-arrays.explanation: An array literal contains empty slots.
eslint:no-sparse-arrays.recommendation: Remove the extra commas or use explicit undefined.
eslint:no-sparse-arrays.severity_rationale: Holes are usually typos and behave inconsistently.
eslint:no-sparse-arrays.title: Sparse array literal

eslint:no-unreachable.recommendation: Remove the dead code or fix the control flow.
eslint:no-unreachable.title: Unreachable code

eslint:no-unsafe-finally.explanation: A control-flow statement inside finally discards exceptions or results.
eslint:no-unsafe-finally.recommendation: Move the control flow out of the finally block.
eslint:no-unsafe-finally.severity_rationale: return/throw in finally overrides the try/catch outcome.
eslint:no-unsafe-finally.title: Control flow in finally

eslint:no-unsafe-negation.explanation: The negation applies to the left operand of in/instanceof.
eslint:no-unsafe-negation.severity_rationale: !a in b negates a, not the in/instanceof result.
eslint:no-unsafe-negation.title: Unsafe negation of left operand

eslint:no-unused-vars.explanation: A variable, function or parameter is declared but never used.
eslint:no-unused-vars.recommendation: Remove it or use it as intended.
eslint:no-unused-vars.severity_rationale: Dead code; may indicate incomplete logic.
eslint:no-unused-vars.title: Unused variable

eslint:no-var.explanation: var is used instead of let/const.
eslint:no-var.severity_rationale: Function scoping and hoisting cause subtle bugs.
eslint:no-var.title: var declaration

eslint:prefer-const.explanation: A let-declared variable is never reassigned.
eslint:prefer-const.severity_rationale: const communicates intent and prevents accidental reassignment.
eslint:prefer-const.title: let that is never reassigned

eslint:use-isnan.explanation: A value is compared with NaN using an equality operator.
eslint:use-isnan.severity_rationale: NaN is never equal to anything, including itself.
eslint:use-isnan.title: Comparison with NaN

eslint:valid-typeof.explanation: typeof is compared with a string that is not a valid type name.
eslint:valid-typeof.severity_rationale: typeof never returns the compared string; the check is always false.
eslint:valid-typeof.title: Invalid typeof comparison

frameworks:crp.sap.extension.dependency-.explanation: extensioninfo.xml files of this upload declare requires-extension entries that form a cycle.
frameworks:crp.sap.extension.dependency-.recommendation: Break the cycle: move the shared code into a separate extension that both depend on, or invert one dependency (for example through a Spring interface defined in the lower extension).
frameworks:crp.sap.extension.dependency-.severity_rationale: The platform cannot determine a load order for extensions in a cycle, so the build or startup fails or behaves unpredictably.
frameworks:crp.sap.extension.dependency-.title: Extensions require each other

frameworks:crp.sf.metadata.retired-api-v.explanation: A metadata file (apiVersion) or sfdx-project.json (sourceApiVersion) declares an API version in the retired range 21.0-30.0.
frameworks:crp.sf.metadata.retired-api-v.recommendation: Raise the version to a supported release, re-run the Apex tests, and check release notes for behaviour that changed between the versions (for example security enforcement and SOQL semantics). Also check integrations that call the org with the old version.
frameworks:crp.sf.metadata.retired-api-v.severity_rationale: Salesforce retired Platform API versions 21.0 through 30.0 in Summer '25: calls at these versions fail, and components pinned to them keep legacy behaviour and miss later platform fixes.
frameworks:crp.sf.metadata.retired-api-v.title: Retired Salesforce API version

nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.no-readiness-probe.explanation: A container that declares a port has no readiness probe, so Kubernetes sends it traffic as soon as the process starts, and keeps sending traffic when it cannot serve.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.no-readiness-probe.recommendation: Add a readinessProbe that checks the application can serve requests (for Spring Boot, /actuator/health/readiness with management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true). Keep it cheap and independent of downstream services.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.no-readiness-probe.severity_rationale: Without readiness, rollouts and restarts route requests to instances that are not ready, which users see as errors; Kubernetes documents readiness probes as the mechanism that gates traffic.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.no-readiness-probe.title: Container without a readiness probe

nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.recreate-strategy.explanation: The Deployment uses strategy type Recreate: all existing instances are stopped before new ones start.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.recreate-strategy.recommendation: Use the default RollingUpdate strategy (with readiness probes and maxUnavailable 0) unless two versions truly cannot run side by side; if they cannot, document the planned downtime.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.recreate-strategy.severity_rationale: Recreate causes downtime on every deployment by design; low because some workloads need it (for example a single-writer volume).
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.recreate-strategy.title: Deployment stops everything on each release

nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.single-replica.explanation: A Kubernetes Deployment or StatefulSet in the upload can run with fewer than two instances: replicas is 1 or not set, and no overlay, kustomization or autoscaler in the upload sets a minimum of two or more.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.single-replica.recommendation: Run at least two replicas (or set the autoscaler's minReplicas to 2 or more), spread them across nodes or zones, and add a PodDisruptionBudget so maintenance never stops every instance. If another repository sets the replica count, record it in the NFR questionnaire.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.single-replica.severity_rationale: With one instance, every crash, node failure, eviction or rollout is an outage; Kubernetes' own guidance runs multiple replicas for availability. Medium because the deployed value may be set outside the upload.
nfr:crp.nfr.k8s.single-replica.title: Workload runs a single instance

nfr:crp.nfr.spring.actuator-exposed.explanation: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include exposes heapdump, env, configprops or threaddump (directly or with *) over HTTP.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.actuator-exposed.recommendation: Expose only health and info over HTTP (management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info); if more endpoints are needed, put them on a separate management port reachable only from inside the network, and require authentication for all of them.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.actuator-exposed.severity_rationale: Spring Boot's documentation warns that endpoints may contain sensitive information; a heap dump contains secrets held in memory. Medium because authentication or network rules outside the configuration may protect them.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.actuator-exposed.title: Sensitive Actuator endpoints exposed over HTTP

nfr:crp.nfr.spring.health-details-public.explanation: management.endpoint.health.show-details=always shows the status and details of every health component (databases, disk space, external services) to any caller.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.health-details-public.recommendation: Use show-details=when-authorized (with roles) or never; probes only need the overall status.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.health-details-public.severity_rationale: Information disclosure that helps an attacker map dependencies and their failures; low because it reveals no credentials by itself.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.health-details-public.title: Health details shown to everyone

nfr:crp.nfr.spring.schema-auto-update.explanation: spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto (or hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto) is create, create-drop or update outside a development or test profile, so Hibernate changes the schema when the application starts.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.schema-auto-update.recommendation: Manage the schema with versioned migrations (Flyway or Liquibase) and set ddl-auto to validate or none for every shared environment.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.schema-auto-update.severity_rationale: create and create-drop delete all data at startup (reported as high); update applies unreviewed changes that cannot be rolled back and never removes or fixes columns. Spring Boot's documentation recommends a migration tool for production databases.
nfr:crp.nfr.spring.schema-auto-update.title: Database schema changed automatically at startup

opengrep:crp.java.command-injection.runt.explanation: Runtime.exec() receives a command string built at runtime; a single string is split on spaces and shell metacharacters in arguments can change what runs.
opengrep:crp.java.command-injection.runt.recommendation: Use ProcessBuilder with a fixed executable and a list of validated arguments; never pass concatenated input.
opengrep:crp.java.command-injection.runt.severity_rationale: Arbitrary command execution on the host if the input is attacker-controlled.
opengrep:crp.java.command-injection.runt.title: OS command built from input (Runtime.exec)

opengrep:crp.java.config.hardcoded-envir.explanation: A URL pointing to a local, test, QA, stage or internal host is written into the code.
opengrep:crp.java.config.hardcoded-envir.recommendation: Read the endpoint from configuration (for example ConfigurationService or Spring properties) with a per-environment value, and fail clearly when it is missing.
opengrep:crp.java.config.hardcoded-envir.severity_rationale: The same build behaves differently per environment only if configuration changes; a compiled URL ties it to one environment.
opengrep:crp.java.config.hardcoded-envir.title: Environment URL hard-coded

opengrep:crp.java.crypto.ecb-mode.explanation: Cipher.getInstance("AES") defaults to ECB, or ECB is requested explicitly.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.ecb-mode.recommendation: Use an authenticated mode such as AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random nonce per message.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.ecb-mode.severity_rationale: ECB encrypts identical blocks identically, revealing patterns in the plaintext.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.ecb-mode.title: Cipher in ECB mode

opengrep:crp.java.crypto.hardcoded-key.explanation: A SecretKeySpec is created from a string literal in source code.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.hardcoded-key.recommendation: Load keys from a secret manager or protected configuration and rotate the exposed key.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.hardcoded-key.severity_rationale: Keys in source are exposed to anyone with repository access and cannot be rotated.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.hardcoded-key.title: Hard-coded cryptographic key

opengrep:crp.java.crypto.weak-hash.explanation: MessageDigest is created for a broken algorithm.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.weak-hash.recommendation: Use SHA-256 or stronger; for passwords use a dedicated KDF (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2, PBKDF2).
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.weak-hash.severity_rationale: Collision attacks make MD5/SHA-1 unsuitable for integrity or signatures.
opengrep:crp.java.crypto.weak-hash.title: Weak hash algorithm (MD5/SHA-1)

opengrep:crp.java.logging.sensitive-data.explanation: A log call includes a variable whose name suggests a password, secret, token, API key, card number, CVV or IBAN.
opengrep:crp.java.logging.sensitive-data.recommendation: Remove the value from the message or log a masked form (for example the last four digits). Check existing logs and rotate any exposed credentials.
opengrep:crp.java.logging.sensitive-data.severity_rationale: Logs are copied to many systems and people; passwords, tokens or card numbers in them are effectively disclosed.
opengrep:crp.java.logging.sensitive-data.title: Sensitive value written to a log

opengrep:crp.java.sql-injection.string-c.explanation: A query is assembled with + and executed, so input becomes part of the SQL syntax.
opengrep:crp.java.sql-injection.string-c.recommendation: Use PreparedStatement with ? placeholders and setX() bindings; validate identifiers against an allowlist.
opengrep:crp.java.sql-injection.string-c.severity_rationale: Attacker-controlled input can change the SQL statement (data theft or modification).
opengrep:crp.java.sql-injection.string-c.title: SQL built by string concatenation

opengrep:crp.js.code-injection.eval.explanation: eval() runs a string as JavaScript with the caller's privileges.
opengrep:crp.js.code-injection.eval.recommendation: Remove eval; use JSON.parse, lookup tables or explicit functions.
opengrep:crp.js.code-injection.eval.severity_rationale: Executes arbitrary strings as code; injection risk.
opengrep:crp.js.code-injection.eval.title: Use of eval()

opengrep:crp.js.command-injection.child-.explanation: child_process.exec/execSync runs the command through a shell and the command string is built at runtime.
opengrep:crp.js.command-injection.child-.recommendation: Use execFile/spawn with a fixed executable and an argument array; validate inputs.
opengrep:crp.js.command-injection.child-.severity_rationale: Arbitrary command execution on the server if the input is attacker-controlled.
opengrep:crp.js.command-injection.child-.title: OS command built from input (child_process)

opengrep:crp.js.secrets.hardcoded-jwt-se.explanation: jwt.sign/verify uses a secret literal embedded in source code.
opengrep:crp.js.secrets.hardcoded-jwt-se.recommendation: Load the signing secret from a secret manager or environment at runtime and rotate the exposed secret.
opengrep:crp.js.secrets.hardcoded-jwt-se.severity_rationale: Anyone with the code can forge valid tokens.
opengrep:crp.js.secrets.hardcoded-jwt-se.title: Hard-coded JWT secret

opengrep:crp.js.xss.document-write.recommendation: Create elements with DOM APIs and set textContent instead.
opengrep:crp.js.xss.document-write.severity_rationale: document.write with untrusted data is a DOM XSS sink and blocks parsing.
opengrep:crp.js.xss.document-write.title: document.write with dynamic content

opengrep:crp.js.xss.inner-html.explanation: A non-literal value is written to an HTML sink.
opengrep:crp.js.xss.inner-html.recommendation: Use textContent, or sanitize with a vetted library (e.g. DOMPurify) before inserting HTML.
opengrep:crp.js.xss.inner-html.severity_rationale: Untrusted strings rendered as HTML enable DOM-based cross-site scripting.
opengrep:crp.js.xss.inner-html.title: Dynamic HTML assigned to innerHTML/outerHTML

opengrep:crp.sap.cronjob.missing-abort-c.explanation: A job's perform() loops over work items without calling clearAbortRequestedIfNeeded(). This is a candidate: short fixed loops are fine.
opengrep:crp.sap.cronjob.missing-abort-c.recommendation: Make the job abortable (isAbortable() returns true), check clearAbortRequestedIfNeeded(cronJob) inside long loops, and process work in idempotent batches that can resume safely.
opengrep:crp.sap.cronjob.missing-abort-c.severity_rationale: A long job that ignores abort requests keeps running during deployments or incidents and may redo work after a restart.
opengrep:crp.sap.cronjob.missing-abort-c.title: Job loop cannot be aborted

opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.string-c.explanation: A FlexibleSearch query string is assembled with + from a variable, so a value from a request or import becomes part of the query syntax.
opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.string-c.recommendation: Use ?parameters in the query and FlexibleSearchQuery.addQueryParameter()/addQueryParameters(); never concatenate user-controlled values. Validate identifiers such as sort fields against an allowlist.
opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.string-c.severity_rationale: Input can change the FlexibleSearch statement, which the platform translates to SQL (data theft or modification).
opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.string-c.title: FlexibleSearch built by string concatenation

opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.unbounde.explanation: A FlexibleSearch result is materialized without setCount()/setStart(). This is a candidate: it matters only when the result can grow with data volume.
opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.unbounde.recommendation: If the result is not naturally small (for example a lookup by unique code), page it with setCount()/setStart(), use a paginated search service, or stream through batches. Confirm the expected size with production-like data before changing working code.
opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.unbounde.severity_rationale: Unbounded results are loaded into memory; with production data volumes this can exhaust the heap or slow storefront pages.
opengrep:crp.sap.flexiblesearch.unbounde.title: FlexibleSearch result without paging

opengrep:crp.sap.interceptor.persisting-.explanation: A prepare, validate, remove or init-defaults interceptor calls ModelService.save/remove. Interceptors run inside another save; persisting from there re-enters the model lifecycle.
opengrep:crp.sap.interceptor.persisting-.recommendation: Change only the intercepted model's own fields (the outer operation saves them). For related models, use InterceptorContext.registerElementFor(...) instead of ModelService.save()/remove(), as SAP's interceptor documentation advises, or move the side effect to an after-save event listener or business process.
opengrep:crp.sap.interceptor.persisting-.severity_rationale: Saving from inside the save cycle can recurse, run other interceptors unexpectedly or persist partial state if the outer save fails.
opengrep:crp.sap.interceptor.persisting-.title: Interceptor saves or removes models

opengrep:crp.sap.jalo.deprecated-api.explanation: Custom code imports de.hybris.platform.jalo classes or calls JaloSession.getCurrentSession(). Generated sources (gensrc, Generated* classes) are not reported.
opengrep:crp.sap.jalo.deprecated-api.recommendation: Use the ServiceLayer: models with ModelService, FlexibleSearchService, UserService, SessionService and CommonI18NService. Migrate one call path at a time and keep behaviour covered by tests.
opengrep:crp.sap.jalo.deprecated-api.severity_rationale: The Jalo layer is SAP's legacy layer; it bypasses the ServiceLayer interceptors and validators that current code and ImpEx rely on.
opengrep:crp.sap.jalo.deprecated-api.title: Jalo layer used in custom code

opengrep:crp.sap.model.save-in-loop.explanation: ModelService.save() or remove() is called once per iteration, so a batch of N items causes N persistence cycles.
opengrep:crp.sap.model.save-in-loop.recommendation: Collect the changed models and call saveAll()/removeAll() once, or process large sets in bounded batches. Keep per-item saves only where each item must commit independently, and document why.
opengrep:crp.sap.model.save-in-loop.severity_rationale: Each save() is a separate persistence round trip (interceptors, flush, cache invalidation), multiplied by the loop size.
opengrep:crp.sap.model.save-in-loop.title: Model saved inside a loop

pmd-apex:ApexCRUDViolation.explanation: A query or DML statement runs without an object/field permission check or user mode.
pmd-apex:ApexCRUDViolation.recommendation: Decide the intended execution context first. For code acting on behalf of the user, use user-mode operations where your API version supports them (WITH USER_MODE, AccessLevel.USER_MODE) or Security.stripInaccessible; otherwise check Schema describe permissions. Code that must run as the system (for example integrations) should document that decision instead of adding checks that change business behaviour.
pmd-apex:ApexCRUDViolation.severity_rationale: Code running in system context can read or change records and fields the user is not allowed to access.
pmd-apex:ApexCRUDViolation.title: Data access without CRUD/FLS enforcement

pmd-apex:ApexInsecureEndpoint.explanation: An HTTP callout endpoint uses http:// instead of https://.
pmd-apex:ApexInsecureEndpoint.recommendation: Use https:// (ideally through a Named Credential) and make sure the remote site or credential configuration also requires TLS.
pmd-apex:ApexInsecureEndpoint.severity_rationale: Data sent over plain HTTP can be read or changed in transit.
pmd-apex:ApexInsecureEndpoint.title: Callout to an unencrypted endpoint

pmd-apex:ApexSOQLInjection.explanation: A variable is concatenated into a string passed to Database.query().
pmd-apex:ApexSOQLInjection.recommendation: Use static SOQL with bind variables, or Database.queryWithBinds(); if dynamic identifiers are unavoidable, check them against an allowlist and escape values with String.escapeSingleQuotes().
pmd-apex:ApexSOQLInjection.severity_rationale: Input concatenated into dynamic SOQL can change the query and expose or filter records the user should not see.
pmd-apex:ApexSOQLInjection.title: Dynamic SOQL built from input

pmd-apex:ApexSharingViolations.explanation: A class that runs queries or DML does not declare with sharing, without sharing or inherited sharing.
pmd-apex:ApexSharingViolations.recommendation: Declare the intended sharing explicitly: with sharing for user-facing logic, inherited sharing for utilities, without sharing only where required and documented.
pmd-apex:ApexSharingViolations.severity_rationale: Without an explicit keyword the class inherits the caller's sharing, which can mean system-wide record access.
pmd-apex:ApexSharingViolations.title: Class without a sharing declaration

pmd-apex:ApexSuggestUsingNamedCred.explanation: An HTTP callout sets an Authorization header from values assembled in Apex.
pmd-apex:ApexSuggestUsingNamedCred.recommendation: Use a Named Credential (with an External Credential) so Salesforce stores and injects the secret; reference it as callout:Name in the endpoint.
pmd-apex:ApexSuggestUsingNamedCred.severity_rationale: Credentials handled in Apex end up in code, custom settings or logs and are hard to rotate.
pmd-apex:ApexSuggestUsingNamedCred.title: Credential built in code for a callout

pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestClassShouldHaveAsse.explanation: A test method runs code but never asserts its outcome.
pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestClassShouldHaveAsse.recommendation: Assert the expected result with the Assert class (for example Assert.areEqual with a message) after Test.stopTest().
pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestClassShouldHaveAsse.severity_rationale: A test without assertions only raises coverage; it cannot detect wrong results.
pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestClassShouldHaveAsse.title: Test without assertions

pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestShouldNotUseSeeAllD.explanation: A test class or method is annotated @isTest(SeeAllData=true).
pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestShouldNotUseSeeAllD.recommendation: Create the test data inside the test (a test data factory or @TestSetup) and remove SeeAllData=true.
pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestShouldNotUseSeeAllD.severity_rationale: Tests that read real org data pass or fail depending on the org and can change real-looking records.
pmd-apex:ApexUnitTestShouldNotUseSeeAllD.title: Test uses org data (SeeAllData=true)

pmd-apex:AvoidNonRestrictiveQueries.explanation: A SOQL/SOSL query has neither a WHERE clause nor a LIMIT.
pmd-apex:AvoidNonRestrictiveQueries.recommendation: Filter on what you actually need and add a LIMIT, or use Batch Apex / a QueryLocator when the full set is really required.
pmd-apex:AvoidNonRestrictiveQueries.severity_rationale: The query returns every record of the object; with growing data it hits the 50,000-row limit or heap limits.
pmd-apex:AvoidNonRestrictiveQueries.title: Query without WHERE or LIMIT

pmd-apex:OperationWithHighCostInLoop.explanation: A costly operation such as Schema.getGlobalDescribe() runs on every loop iteration.
pmd-apex:OperationWithHighCostInLoop.recommendation: Call it once before the loop and reuse the result (for example a Map of SObjectTypes).
pmd-apex:OperationWithHighCostInLoop.severity_rationale: Describe calls are slow and count toward CPU time; repeating them per record can exceed the CPU limit.
pmd-apex:OperationWithHighCostInLoop.title: Expensive call inside a loop

pmd-apex:OperationWithLimitsInLoop.explanation: A SOQL/SOSL query, DML statement or other limited operation runs once per loop iteration, so the code breaks on bulk loads, data imports and triggers with many records.
pmd-apex:OperationWithLimitsInLoop.recommendation: Bulkify: collect IDs first, run one query with IN :ids before the loop, and perform one DML statement on a list after the loop.
pmd-apex:OperationWithLimitsInLoop.severity_rationale: Governor limits (100 SOQL queries, 150 DML statements per transaction) are exceeded as soon as enough records are processed together.
pmd-apex:OperationWithLimitsInLoop.title: Query or DML inside a loop

pmd-apex:QueueableWithoutFinalizer.explanation: A Queueable implementation does not attach a Finalizer (System.attachFinalizer) to handle failures.
pmd-apex:QueueableWithoutFinalizer.recommendation: Attach a Finalizer that logs failures, alerts or re-enqueues with a bounded retry count, where the job's outcome matters.
pmd-apex:QueueableWithoutFinalizer.severity_rationale: Failures in asynchronous jobs go unnoticed unless something records or retries them.
pmd-apex:QueueableWithoutFinalizer.title: Queueable job without a finalizer

pmd:AssignmentInOperand.explanation: An assignment is performed inside a condition or larger expression.
pmd:AssignmentInOperand.recommendation: Move the assignment to its own statement.
pmd:AssignmentInOperand.severity_rationale: Hard to read; easily mistaken for comparison.
pmd:AssignmentInOperand.title: Assignment inside an operand

pmd:AvoidDecimalLiteralsInBigDecimalCons.explanation: Decimal literals are converted to double before BigDecimal sees them.
pmd:AvoidDecimalLiteralsInBigDecimalCons.severity_rationale: new BigDecimal(0.1) captures binary floating-point error.
pmd:AvoidDecimalLiteralsInBigDecimalCons.title: Imprecise BigDecimal construction

pmd:AvoidPrintStackTrace.explanation: Throwable.printStackTrace() writes to standard error, bypassing the logging framework, levels and redaction.
pmd:AvoidPrintStackTrace.recommendation: Log the exception through the application logger with context, or rethrow it.
pmd:AvoidPrintStackTrace.severity_rationale: Stack traces bypass log routing and may leak internals to consoles.
pmd:AvoidPrintStackTrace.title: printStackTrace instead of logging

pmd:AvoidReassigningParameters.explanation: A method parameter is reassigned inside the method body.
pmd:AvoidReassigningParameters.recommendation: Assign to a new local variable instead.
pmd:AvoidReassigningParameters.severity_rationale: Reduces readability; can hide logic errors.
pmd:AvoidReassigningParameters.title: Reassigned method parameter

pmd:AvoidThrowingRawExceptionTypes.explanation: RuntimeException, Exception or Throwable is thrown directly.
pmd:AvoidThrowingRawExceptionTypes.recommendation: Throw a specific or custom exception type.
pmd:AvoidThrowingRawExceptionTypes.title: Raw exception type thrown

pmd:BigIntegerInstantiation.explanation: Constants such as BigInteger.ONE already exist.
pmd:BigIntegerInstantiation.recommendation: Use the provided constants (ZERO, ONE, TEN).
pmd:BigIntegerInstantiation.title: Unnecessary BigInteger/BigDecimal instantiation

pmd:BrokenNullCheck.explanation: The null check is combined with the wrong operator so the dereference still executes when null.
pmd:BrokenNullCheck.recommendation: Fix the boolean operator (&& vs ||) so the dereference only runs for non-null values.
pmd:BrokenNullCheck.severity_rationale: The check itself throws NullPointerException or never protects the dereference.
pmd:BrokenNullCheck.title: Broken null check

pmd:CloseResource.explanation: A closeable resource (stream, connection, statement) is not guaranteed to be closed on all paths.
pmd:CloseResource.recommendation: Use try-with-resources so the resource is closed on every path.
pmd:CloseResource.severity_rationale: Leaked streams/connections exhaust file handles or pools under load.
pmd:CloseResource.title: Resource not closed

pmd:CollapsibleIfStatements.explanation: Nested if statements without else can be combined with &&.
pmd:CollapsibleIfStatements.title: Collapsible if statements

pmd:CompareObjectsWithEquals.explanation: == compares object identity, not value equality.
pmd:CompareObjectsWithEquals.recommendation: Use equals() (or Objects.equals) unless identity comparison is intended.
pmd:CompareObjectsWithEquals.severity_rationale: Identity comparison usually produces wrong results for value objects.
pmd:CompareObjectsWithEquals.title: Object references compared with ==

pmd:ControlStatementBraces.explanation: if/else/for/while bodies are written without braces.
pmd:ControlStatementBraces.recommendation: Always use braces for control statement bodies.
pmd:ControlStatementBraces.severity_rationale: Increases risk of errors when statements are added later.
pmd:ControlStatementBraces.title: Control statement without braces

pmd:DoubleCheckedLocking.explanation: Lazy initialization uses double-checked locking without a volatile field.
pmd:DoubleCheckedLocking.recommendation: Make the field volatile, or use the holder-class idiom / eager initialization.
pmd:DoubleCheckedLocking.severity_rationale: Other threads may observe a partially constructed object.
pmd:DoubleCheckedLocking.title: Broken double-checked locking

pmd:EmptyCatchBlock.explanation: An exception is caught and ignored without handling, logging or a documented reason.
pmd:EmptyCatchBlock.recommendation: Handle, log or rethrow the exception; if ignoring is intentional, document why and narrow the caught type.
pmd:EmptyCatchBlock.severity_rationale: Silently swallowed exceptions hide failures and corrupt state.
pmd:EmptyCatchBlock.title: Empty catch block

pmd:EmptyControlStatement.explanation: A control statement (if/while/for/try) has an empty body.
pmd:EmptyControlStatement.recommendation: Remove it or implement the intended logic.
pmd:EmptyControlStatement.severity_rationale: Often an unfinished branch or stray semicolon.
pmd:EmptyControlStatement.title: Empty control statement

pmd:EqualsNull.explanation: x.equals(null) returns false or throws NullPointerException when x is null.
pmd:EqualsNull.severity_rationale: Always false or throws; never a correct null check.
pmd:EqualsNull.title: equals(null) comparison

pmd:HardCodedCryptoKey.explanation: A cryptographic key is constructed from a literal embedded in source code.
pmd:HardCodedCryptoKey.recommendation: Load keys from a secret manager or protected configuration and rotate the exposed key.
pmd:HardCodedCryptoKey.severity_rationale: Keys in source are exposed to anyone with repository access and cannot be rotated.
pmd:HardCodedCryptoKey.title: Hard-coded cryptographic key

pmd:ImplicitSwitchFallThrough.explanation: A non-empty switch case falls through to the next case without break/return.
pmd:ImplicitSwitchFallThrough.recommendation: Add break/return, or document intentional fall-through.
pmd:ImplicitSwitchFallThrough.severity_rationale: Unintended execution of the next case.
pmd:ImplicitSwitchFallThrough.title: Implicit switch fall-through

pmd:InefficientStringBuffering.explanation: String concatenation is passed to append(), creating temporary strings.
pmd:InefficientStringBuffering.severity_rationale: Defeats the purpose of the builder.
pmd:InefficientStringBuffering.title: Concatenation inside StringBuilder.append

pmd:InsecureCryptoIv.explanation: An IvParameterSpec is built from constant bytes.
pmd:InsecureCryptoIv.recommendation: Generate a random IV per encryption (SecureRandom) and store it with the ciphertext.
pmd:InsecureCryptoIv.severity_rationale: A static IV breaks confidentiality guarantees for many cipher modes.
pmd:InsecureCryptoIv.title: Hard-coded initialization vector

pmd:JumbledIncrementer.explanation: A nested loop increments the outer loop's variable.
pmd:JumbledIncrementer.recommendation: Increment the loop's own control variable.
pmd:JumbledIncrementer.title: Wrong loop variable incremented

pmd:LiteralsFirstInComparisons.explanation: The comparison calls equals/compareTo on a variable with a literal argument; if the variable is null this throws.
pmd:LiteralsFirstInComparisons.recommendation: Put the literal first ("x".equals(value)) or use Objects.equals.
pmd:LiteralsFirstInComparisons.severity_rationale: Calling equals on a possibly-null reference can throw at runtime.
pmd:LiteralsFirstInComparisons.title: Possible NullPointerException in comparison

pmd:MisplacedNullCheck.explanation: The null check appears after the object is already used in the same expression.
pmd:MisplacedNullCheck.recommendation: Check for null before the first dereference.
pmd:MisplacedNullCheck.severity_rationale: The value is dereferenced before it is checked for null.
pmd:MisplacedNullCheck.title: Null check after dereference

pmd:PreserveStackTrace.explanation: A new exception is thrown in a catch block without passing the caught exception as its cause.
pmd:PreserveStackTrace.recommendation: Pass the caught exception as the cause: throw new XException(msg, e).
pmd:PreserveStackTrace.severity_rationale: Losing the original cause hinders diagnosis of production failures.
pmd:PreserveStackTrace.title: Exception cause not preserved

pmd:ReturnEmptyCollectionRatherThanNull.explanation: A method with a collection/array return type returns null.
pmd:ReturnEmptyCollectionRatherThanNull.recommendation: Return an empty collection or array (e.g. List.of()).
pmd:ReturnEmptyCollectionRatherThanNull.severity_rationale: Callers commonly iterate without null checks, causing NPEs.
pmd:ReturnEmptyCollectionRatherThanNull.title: Null returned instead of empty collection

pmd:ReturnFromFinallyBlock.explanation: A return in a finally block overrides any exception thrown or value returned in try/catch.
pmd:ReturnFromFinallyBlock.recommendation: Move the return out of the finally block.
pmd:ReturnFromFinallyBlock.severity_rationale: Discards exceptions and earlier return values.
pmd:ReturnFromFinallyBlock.title: return inside finally

pmd:SimplifyBooleanReturns.explanation: An if/else returns boolean literals that could be returned directly.
pmd:SimplifyBooleanReturns.title: Boolean return can be simplified

pmd:SystemPrintln.explanation: Direct console output is not structured, levelled or redacted.
pmd:SystemPrintln.title: System.out / System.err usage

pmd:UnusedFormalParameter.explanation: A parameter of a private method or constructor is never used.
pmd:UnusedFormalParameter.recommendation: Remove the parameter and update callers, or use it as intended.
pmd:UnusedFormalParameter.severity_rationale: Misleading API surface; no direct runtime effect.
pmd:UnusedFormalParameter.title: Unused method parameter

pmd:UnusedLocalVariable.explanation: A local variable is assigned but its value is never read, which usually indicates leftover or incomplete logic.
pmd:UnusedLocalVariable.recommendation: Remove the variable or use its value; if the call is needed for side effects, call it without assignment.
pmd:UnusedLocalVariable.severity_rationale: Dead code; no runtime impact on its own.
pmd:UnusedLocalVariable.title: Unused local variable

pmd:UnusedPrivateField.explanation: A private field is declared but never read.
pmd:UnusedPrivateField.recommendation: Remove the field or use it; check for framework/serialization access before deleting.
pmd:UnusedPrivateField.title: Unused private field

pmd:UnusedPrivateMethod.explanation: A private method is never called from within its class.
pmd:UnusedPrivateMethod.recommendation: Delete the method or wire it into the intended call path; confirm it is not invoked reflectively or by a framework.
pmd:UnusedPrivateMethod.title: Unused private method

pmd:UseCollectionIsEmpty.explanation: size() == 0 is less expressive and can be slower for some collections.
pmd:UseCollectionIsEmpty.title: Use isEmpty() instead of size() comparison

pmd:UseEqualsToCompareStrings.explanation: == on String compares references; equal strings from different sources are not identical.
pmd:UseEqualsToCompareStrings.severity_rationale: String identity comparison gives inconsistent results at runtime.
pmd:UseEqualsToCompareStrings.title: Strings compared with ==

pmd:UseIndexOfChar.explanation: indexOf("x") is used where indexOf('x') suffices.
pmd:UseIndexOfChar.severity_rationale: Slightly slower than the char overload.
pmd:UseIndexOfChar.title: indexOf with single-character String

pmd:UseStringBufferForStringAppends.explanation: Repeated += on String allocates a new object each time.
pmd:UseStringBufferForStringAppends.title: String concatenation with += in a loop or repeatedly

smells:crp.arch.cycle.explanation: Parts of the code (Java packages or folders) depend on each other in a circle, so none of them can be changed, tested or released without the others. Potential: found in the code structure, not confirmed at run time.
smells:crp.arch.cycle.recommendation: Break the cycle where it is cheapest (the finding names those dependencies): move the shared code into a part both may use, or invert one dependency with an interface owned by the part that should stay independent.
smells:crp.arch.cycle.severity_rationale: Cycles tie parts together and spread every change across them (R. C. Martin's Acyclic Dependencies Principle); they rarely break anything on their own.
smells:crp.arch.cycle.title: Dependency cycle between parts

smells:crp.arch.hub.explanation: A part is used by many parts and uses many parts, so changes reach it from all sides and spread from it to all sides. Potential: found in the code structure.
smells:crp.arch.hub.recommendation: Split the part by responsibility so that each piece has fewer users and fewer dependencies; the busiest files named in the finding are where to start.
smells:crp.arch.hub.severity_rationale: Hubs concentrate change risk and coordination between teams; they rarely break anything on their own.
smells:crp.arch.hub.title: Hub-like part

smells:crp.arch.unstable-dependency.explanation: A part depends on parts that change more easily than itself (higher instability: more outgoing than incoming dependencies), so their changes ripple into it and into everything that depends on it. Potential: found in the code structure.
smells:crp.arch.unstable-dependency.recommendation: Depend in the direction of stability: put the needed contract in a stable part (an interface the unstable part implements), or make the dependency part more stable.
smells:crp.arch.unstable-dependency.severity_rationale: Breaks R. C. Martin's Stable Dependencies Principle; raises the cost of change rather than causing faults.
smells:crp.arch.unstable-dependency.title: Depends on a less stable part
